phoneRisks: 375px: the full navigation card renders above the content (AppShell.tsx:155), so the toolbar starts roughly one screen down
Toolbar wraps into 3-4 rows (select, search, count, Refresh) because everything is flex-wrap with no mobile ordering (104-111)

Rail and detail stack (xl only grid). The rail can be up to 860px tall; tapping a card changes the URL but nothing scrolls the detail into view — the scrollIntoView only targets the rail card (88-94). Users must scroll past the rail to see what they selected
Rail cards are Links styled with hover-only border/background changes (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:447); on touch the only selected cue is the brand border
Refresh button ~38px tall is acceptable, but the select uses native styling with 'text-sm' and no min-height
Search 'min-w-40' (160px) forces a wrap when the select is beside it on a 343px content width
tabletRisks: 768-1279px: still single column — the side-by-side record browser never appears on any tablet, even 1024px landscape, because the split is gated at xl (1280px) while the sidebar appears at lg (1024px), leaving ~740px of content width stacked vertically
At 1024px the sidebar (w-64) plus the stacked 860px rail means the detail pane is far below the fold
Two nested scroll regions (rail overflow-auto, page scroll) make trackpad/touch scrolling ambiguous
desktopNotes: At >=1280px the rail gets minmax(320px,0.7fr) and the detail 1.8fr inside a 1900px max shell — comfortable on 1440+
Rail height is a fixed 860px regardless of viewport; on a 768px-tall laptop the rail exceeds the viewport, so the page and the rail both scroll
Selection state, filters, and search are not persisted in the URL (only :id is), so refresh loses filters

painPoints.issue: Submission index is capped at the first 200 submissions (`/submissions/page?limit=200`); assessments whose submissions fall outside it show 'Submission #id' with no descriptor in the rail, and '—' for status/created/submitted in the detail table, with 'Open' instead of 'Review'. Search also silently misses those submissions. Nothing tells the user data is missing.
Two-column browse layout only exists at xl (>=1280px); on phones and all tablets the rail (up to 860px tall) stacks above the detail and selecting a card does not scroll to the detail.

List loads up to 1000 assessments in one call with no pagination, sorting, or 'load more'; rail order is whatever the server returns and there is no sort control (e.g., by updated date, district, waiting-on).
Deep link to an id that is not in the list (deleted, filtered, or not permitted) silently falls back to the first assessment with no 'not found' message.
Duplicate 'N of M assessments' count in toolbar and rail header.
Filter select and search input have no associated label or aria-label; error banner has no role=alert; loading/empty messages have no aria-live.
Rail card shows 'Office NORTH' / 'D03' while the detail header shows 'North GeoTech Office' / 'District 03' for the same record.
Rail card 'Waiting on' shows the engineer's name only for the selected card (assignments are only known for the loaded detail); other cards show the generic 'Assigned Engineer'.
Permanent read-only banner cannot be dismissed and repeats what the page name and My Work already convey; costs ~60px on phones.
Filters/search are not reflected in the URL, so sharing or refreshing loses them; only :id survives.

strengths: Clear IA: record browsing here, actions in My Work, with a targeted CTA deep link (/my-work?assessment=id) when the step belongs to the viewer (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:269; MyWorkPage.tsx:84-88)
Search covers linked submission descriptors and statuses, not just assessment fields (assessmentModel.ts:142-166), and the model is unit-tested (assessmentModel.test.ts)
Submission summaries are loaded once as an index to avoid N+1 requests, and the page degrades gracefully if that call fails (AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:14-27)
Deep link scrolls the selected rail card into view (88-94); sidebar keeps 'Assessments' active on submission pages (AppShell.tsx:87)
Rail cards and the panel are shared with My Work so the 'Waiting on' vocabulary is identical across both surfaces (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:410-450)
Distinct loading vs empty vs error messaging (124, 142, 118)

screens.name: Assessment detail panel (shared; record mode at /assessments/:id, work mode in /my-work)
screens.route: Component, not a route: rendered by AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:140 with mode='record' and by features/myWork/MyWorkPage.tsx:181 with mode='work' (route /my-work, ProtectedRoute; My Work self-gates on hasWorkQueue)
screens.purpose: Shows one assessment's identity, pipeline position, next step, attached technical submissions, assignments, and history — and in work mode exposes the role-appropriate workflow actions inline.
roles: Record mode: any operational role (via /assessments RoleRoute)

Work mode: operational roles with a queue (MyWorkPage.tsx:117 hasWorkQueue); action visibility per assessmentPermissions (assessmentModel.ts:115-135): delegate = Office Chief/Admin in PENDING_OFFICE_DELEGATION; assignEngineer = Branch Chief/Admin in PENDING_ENGINEER_ASSIGNMENT; submit = assigned engineer/Admin in DRAFT or REVISION_REQUESTED; addSubmission = assigned engineer with GEOTECH_ENGINEER role (or Admin) in engineering step; review = assigned REVIEWER/APPROVER or Admin in SUBMITTED; finalize = Office Chief/Admin in APPROVED; addReviewer = Office Chief/Branch Chief/Admin unless FINALIZED
Role flags derived from utils/roleModel.ts isAdmin, canDelegateBranch, canAssignEngineer, isEngineer (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:151-154)
primaryTasks: Understand the assessment's current state, who it is waiting on, and what happens next
Open the attached technical submission(s) to fill out or review them
(Work mode) Perform the step owned by my role: delegate, assign engineer, submit, approve/request revision, finalize, manage reviewers

entryPoints: Selected via rail card or ?assessment=:id deep link in /my-work (MyWorkPage.tsx:84-88, 160-168, 181)
exits: /submissions/:id (Fill out submission 277; descriptor link 352; Review/Open 357; auto-navigate after creating a draft 285)

responsive.layout: Vertical stack 'grid gap-3.5' of cards (228): header card, next-step card, submissions card (table body 'overflow-x-auto'), assignments card, history card ('max-h-[420px] overflow-auto'). Header uses 'flex flex-wrap items-start justify-between'; all button rows are 'flex flex-wrap'. Pipeline is an <ol> with 'flex items-start overflow-x-auto' and each step 'min-w-[74px]' plus 'min-w-3' connectors (84-105). Work-mode selects are 'min-w-0 flex-1' (129).
breakpointsUsed: None — the panel contains no sm/md/lg/xl classes; it relies entirely on flex-wrap, overflow-x-auto, and the parent's xl grid
Fixed pixels: min-w-[74px] per pipeline step (91), min-w-3 connectors (105), max-h-[420px] history (390)
phoneRisks: Pipeline minimum width is ~504px (6 × 74px + 5 × 12px) against ~311px of card width at 375px, so it scrolls horizontally with no scroll hint; 'Finalized' and 'Approval' steps are off-screen by default (84-105)
Technical submissions table has 7 columns and scrolls horizontally inside its card; the right-aligned 'Action' column (Review/Open) is hidden off-screen (342-343, 336)
All action buttons use 'px-3 py-1.5 text-xs' (~28px tall) and the Add-reviewer select is 'px-2 py-1 text-xs' — below the 44px touch target guideline (126-129, 370)
Work mode: Delegate row places two flex-1 selects plus a button in one flex-wrap row; option text '{name} · {email}' overflows native pickers (296-306)
Header meta line 'Office · District · Updated …' wraps to 2-3 lines; badge drops beneath the title (230-238)
Hover-only affordances: descriptor link changes color only on hover (352); buttons rely on hover:bg — no visible pressed/focus style
History card nested scroll (max-h-[420px]) inside a page that also scrolls
Six link/button pills in the header + next-step CTA all wrap into 2-3 rows
tabletRisks: 768px: the 7-column submissions table still overflows (~800px of natural width) so the Action column requires a horizontal scroll
Pipeline fits from ~600px card width onward, so tablets are fine for it
Because the parent stacks rail above detail until 1280px, the panel sits below up to 860px of rail on every tablet
desktopNotes: At >=1280px the panel gets ~1.8fr of the content width; the table and pipeline fit without scrolling
History card capped at 420px creates a third scroll region alongside the rail and the page

Every selection triggers 1 assessment GET + 1 incident GET (+ up to 3 option GETs in work mode), with no skeleton — the previous record stays on screen until the new one arrives in record mode (AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:73-85)

painPoints.issue: One shared 'Optional workflow notes' textarea feeds six different actions, and destructive/irreversible ones (Request revision, Approve, Finalize, Remove assignment) fire immediately with no confirmation or summary of what note will be attached.

Reviewer comments (the reason for a revision) are buried in the History card's notes box at the bottom of the panel; the 'Next step' card tells the engineer to 'Address the reviewer's comments' without surfacing them.

Technical submissions table: 7 columns with a raw 'User #id' Reporter column, a redundant Action column that duplicates the descriptor link, and silent dashes when the submission is outside the 200-item index.
Pipeline overflows horizontally on phones with no affordance; steps show no dates although the API supplies per-step timestamps.
Pipeline conveys the active step only through color and font weight; no aria-current/text marker; dots are aria-hidden so screen readers get a flat list of 6 labels.
Submission statuses render as raw uppercase codes ('SUBMITTED', 'REJECTED') beside humanized assessment states ('Submitted for review', 'Revision requested').
Two date formats on one screen: 'Sep 5, 2026, 3:04 PM' (header/table/history) vs '09/05/26, 03:04 PM' embedded in the submission descriptor.
Action buttons are ~28px tall (text-xs py-1.5) and have no focus-visible styling of their own; reviewer select is even smaller.
Record-mode explanatory text 'Actions for this step are performed from My Work by the responsible role.' repeats on every non-actionable record in addition to the page-level banner.
Work-mode option fetch errors and action errors are pushed to the parent page's single error banner above the rail — far from the control that failed, and not cleared on success.
Incident title requires a separate /incidents/:id call per selection; until it resolves the title flips from 'Incident #id technical assessment' to 'Incident #id · Title', causing layout shift.
'Review' action styling is applied whenever the submission is SUBMITTED, even for viewers who cannot review (record mode, non-reviewers).
Assignment 'Remove' has no confirmation and the Assignments card gives no cue about who added the reviewer or when (assigned_by_user_id/created_at exist in the API).

strengths: Single component serves both record and work modes, so vocabulary, layout, and state logic never drift between browsing and acting (146, 189-191, 267-273)

'Next step / Waiting on {who}' with a role-specific instruction sentence is a strong coordination pattern, and revision state is visually distinct (red) throughout badge, pipeline, and next-step card (254-265, 88, 224)

Permissions mirror server guards through a pure, unit-tested model (assessmentModel.ts:115-139; assessmentModel.test.ts), and buttons are disabled with helper text rather than hidden when a precondition fails (291, 306, 315, 319)
State-aware empty states (finalized without a form vs engineer will create it) and mode-aware CTAs (339, 267-270)
Rich cross-linking to incident, map, and event group, plus a return path from submission detail back to the assessment (241-243; SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:78-79)
Theme-token driven tones (good/bad/brand/neutral) via color-mix, consistent across light/dark/coastal (64-69; index.css)
Pipeline <ol> carries an aria-label and decorative dots are aria-hidden (84, 93, 105)
Form state resets on assessment/state change and after each action, preventing stale notes from leaking into the next action (171-173, 212)
